lessons.title: At the café
lessons.objective: Ask for a drink with the softened verb quisiera, and keep the accents on café and té.

legacyExercises.prompt: Quiero and quisiera are the same verb. Which request is the softened, polite one?
legacyExercises.explanation: Quisiera gives the verb a conditional ending, and that is what makes the request courteous. Quiero is the blunt form.

legacyExercises.prompt: Ask for tea politely, using the softened verb rather than quiero.
legacyExercises.explanation: Same polite frame, tea instead of coffee: Quisiera un té, por favor, with the accent on té.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the café exchange. How many drinks does the customer order?
legacyExercises.explanation: The customer asks for a té and then adds un café, so two drinks in all.
legacyExercises.passage:
— ¡Buenas! Quisiera un té, por favor.
— ¿Un té?
— Sí, y un café también. Gracias.
legacyExercises.translation:
— Hello! I would like a tea, please.
— A tea?
— Yes, and a coffee too. Thank you.

answers: I would like a coffee, please.
legacyExercises.prompt: What does this café line mean in English: Quisiera un café, por favor.
legacyExercises.explanation: Quisiera is 'I would like', and por favor supplies the 'please'.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order to build the polite request for one coffee.
legacyExercises.explanation: Quisiera opens it, the drink follows with un, and por favor finishes the request.

legacyExercises.prompt: You reach the counter and want a coffee. Make the short polite request, without the verb.
legacyExercises.explanation: Un café, por favor — the short request drops quisiera but keeps por favor.

lessons.culturalNote: A greeting before a request and thanks afterward make this small exchange courteous.

lessons.title: Numbers and quantities
lessons.objective: Count one to ten, then see how Spanish welds a whole number such as veintiuno into a single written word.

legacyExercises.prompt: Three is hiding inside veintitrés, glued to veinte. Which Spanish word is it?
legacyExercises.explanation: Tres is three. The twenties simply glue a number onto veinte, so veintitrés is twenty-three.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the price board. How much is the tea?
legacyExercises.explanation: The board prices tea at tres euros. Dos and tres behave here exactly as they did when you counted.
legacyExercises.passage:
Café: dos euros.
Té: tres euros.
legacyExercises.translation:
Coffee: two euros.
Tea: three euros.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the Spanish words in order to ask the price of one coffee.
legacyExercises.explanation: ¿Cuánto cuesta? is the price question as a unit, and the upside-down question mark opens the sentence. Un café follows it.

legacyExercises.prompt: Say in Spanish: Two apples, please.
legacyExercises.explanation: Manzanas is feminine plural, so 'one' would be una, but two is dos either way, only the word for one changes with the noun.

legacyExercises.prompt: Think: a fruit seller has one apple but no sign. Ask the price in Spanish, then write the question.
legacyExercises.explanation: One apple is una manzana, with the feminine una. The price question itself never changes.

lessons.culturalNote: Prices may be said quickly. First listen for the number, then the item and the total.

lessons.title: Asking the way
lessons.objective: Learn the accent that turns donde into a question, then trace a set of directions step by step.
lessons.culturalNote: In Spain you open a request to a stranger with Perdone, and you thank them even for one sentence of directions.

lessons.title: Prices and paying
lessons.objective: Ask a price inside Spanish's two question marks, and make costar agree with one thing or with several.
lessons.culturalNote: In many Spanish bars the bill comes when you ask for it, so la cuenta, por favor is the normal way to end a meal.

lessons.title: Days and times
lessons.objective: Five Spanish weekdays are the old planets and gods; learn which two days break that pattern.

legacyExercises.prompt: Your Madrid phone writes a label above the date. Tap the label for today.
legacyExercises.explanation: That is hoy. The decoys mean tomorrow, Monday and the week.

legacyExercises.prompt: Build the Spanish sentence for on Monday I work; the article carries the on.
legacyExercises.explanation: El sits in front of the day and means on: el lunes, on Monday.

legacyExercises.prompt: Complete the Spanish for on Mondays, meaning every Monday: ___ lunes trabajo.
legacyExercises.explanation: Spanish uses the plural article for a repeated day: los lunes, on Mondays.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the sentence before you write it: today is Friday.
legacyExercises.explanation: Hoy es plus the day. Viernes still carries the name of Venus.

legacyExercises.prompt: Give the English meaning: El lunes trabajo.
legacyExercises.explanation: There is no separate word for on here; the article el does that work in front of the day.

legacyExercises.prompt: Five Spanish weekdays carry the name of a planet or a god. Which pair leaves that company?
legacyExercises.explanation: Sábado comes from the Sabbath and domingo from the Lord's day; lunes to viernes are the old sky names.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the week. Which day does the passage name after the moon?
legacyExercises.explanation: The first line says it: el lunes is the day of la Luna, the moon.
legacyExercises.passage: El lunes es el día de la Luna. El martes trabajo. El miércoles estudio. El jueves llamo a mi madre. El viernes descanso.
legacyExercises.translation: Monday is the day of the moon. On Tuesday I work. On Wednesday I study. On Thursday I call my mother. On Friday I rest.

lessons.culturalNote: Spanish weekdays are not capitalised, which is why lunes looks the same mid-sentence as at the start of one.

lessons.title: Family and people
lessons.objective: Say how many brothers and sisters you have, and let mi or mis follow the number you name.
lessons.culturalNote: Familia in Spanish often stretches to grandparents, aunts and cousins, not just the household.

lessons.title: Build it: polite requests
lessons.objective: Build polite café requests from their parts, without looking at the frame.

lessons.title: Mission: find the café
lessons.objective: Ask the way to the café, follow directions, and order politely.

lessons.title: Remember the basics
lessons.objective: Retrieve words and phrases from your first four lessons, from memory.

lessons.title: Mission: find the museum
lessons.objective: Ask the way to the museum, buy a ticket, and say thanks.

lessons.title: Mission: the birthday party
lessons.objective: Greet the host, introduce yourself, and introduce your brother and sister.

lessons.title: Build it: my family
lessons.objective: Build sentences about your family from tiles.

lessons.title: Home and articles
lessons.objective: Name the rooms of a home and put the right article — el, la, los, las — in front of every noun.
lessons.culturalNote: Many Spanish homes centre on the salón, the living room where the family eats, talks and watches television together.

lessons.title: Describing things
lessons.objective: Describe things with ser and make the adjective match — alto with el libro, alta with la casa.

legacyExercises.prompt: Mesa is feminine. Which line describes it correctly?
legacyExercises.explanation: Mesa is feminine and singular, so both the article and the adjective stay feminine: la mesa es nueva.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the sentence before you write it: the house is big.
legacyExercises.explanation: Casa is feminine, but grande is one of the adjectives that doesn't change for gender — only for number: La casa es grande.

legacyExercises.prompt: Muy always stands right before the adjective. Choose the correct line.
legacyExercises.explanation: Muy hugs the adjective it strengthens: es muy alto.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: the house is very big.
legacyExercises.explanation: Ser carries the description, and muy stands before grande: La casa es muy grande.

legacyExercises.prompt: Translate into Spanish: They are tall. (masculine)
legacyExercises.explanation: Ser in the plural is son, and alto copies the masculine plural: Son altos.

legacyExercises.prompt: Libro is masculine and singular. Fill the gap: El libro es ___.
legacyExercises.explanation: Libro is masculine and singular, so the adjective stays nuevo: El libro es nuevo.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the description. Which adjective describes the lamp?
legacyExercises.explanation: The last sentence gives it: la lámpara es alta.
legacyExercises.passage: Mi dormitorio es pequeño pero bonito. La cama es nueva y la mesa es grande. El libro de la mesa es muy interesante. La lámpara es alta.
legacyExercises.translation: My bedroom is small but pretty. The bed is new and the table is big. The book on the table is very interesting. The lamp is tall.

lessons.culturalNote: Spanish puts most adjectives after the noun — la casa grande — which is why the description always comes last.

lessons.title: More than one
lessons.objective: Make plurals the Spanish way — add -s after a vowel, -es after a consonant.
lessons.culturalNote: Spanish plurals are wonderfully regular compared to English: no mice or children to memorise, just -s and -es.

lessons.title: Work and daily routine
lessons.objective: Talk about your day with trabajar and estudiar, and place it with por la mañana, por la tarde, por la noche.
lessons.culturalNote: In Spain the working day often pauses for a long midday break, so por la tarde can start surprisingly late.

lessons.title: Saying no
lessons.objective: Say no and not in Spanish — no goes right before the verb — and add nunca, nada and nadie.
lessons.culturalNote: Spanish happily doubles its negatives — No como nada — where English would call it a double negative.

lessons.title: Asking questions
lessons.objective: Ask with qué, quién, dónde, cuándo and cómo — and remember the accent marks.
lessons.culturalNote: Spanish writes the question twice — ¿ at the start and ? at the end — so the reader hears the question coming.

lessons.title: Food and drink
lessons.objective: Talk about food with comer and beber, and say what you like with me gusta.
lessons.culturalNote: In Spain lunch is the big meal of the day, often eaten well after 2 p.m.

lessons.title: Mine and yours
lessons.objective: Say whose it is with mi, tu and su — and make them plural with mis, tus, sus.
lessons.culturalNote: Spanish skips the article before a possessive — mi casa, not la mi casa.

lessons.title: Getting around
lessons.objective: Say how you get around with ir — voy, vas, va — and en coche, en metro, a pie.
lessons.culturalNote: Spanish cities run on the metro and on foot; a pie is a point of pride, not a fallback.

lessons.title: Polite requests
lessons.objective: Ask politely with poder and querer — and soften everything with querría.
lessons.culturalNote: Querría turns a demand into a request; in a Spanish bar it is the difference between ordering and asking.

lessons.title: Yesterday: a first look at the past
lessons.objective: Take a first step into the past with hablé, comí — and the mighty fue.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which line says I spoke with Ana yesterday?
legacyExercises.explanation: The -é ending with its accent is the I form of the past: Ayer hablé con Ana.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the sentence before you write it: I ate bread.
legacyExercises.explanation: Comer is an -er verb, so the I past ends in -í: Comí pan.

legacyExercises.prompt: Fue means was here. Choose the correct line.
legacyExercises.explanation: Fue already means was — no helper verb needed: La película fue muy buena.
options: La película es fue muy buena.
La película era fue muy buena.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: last night I studied Spanish.
legacyExercises.explanation: Time first, then the past verb: Anoche estudié español.

legacyExercises.prompt: Translate into Spanish: Yesterday I worked a lot.
legacyExercises.explanation: Ayer sets the past, and trabajé carries the accent: Ayer trabajé mucho.

legacyExercises.prompt: The subject is yo, so the past of hablar ends in -é. Fill the gap: Ayer ___ con mi madre.
legacyExercises.explanation: The I past of hablar is hablé: Ayer hablé con mi madre.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read about yesterday. Who did the writer speak with?
legacyExercises.explanation: The third sentence names her: hablé con Ana.
legacyExercises.passage: Ayer fue un día perfecto. Comí con mi familia. Por la tarde hablé con Ana. Anoche estudié un poco y dormí bien.
legacyExercises.translation: Yesterday was a perfect day. I ate with my family. In the afternoon I spoke with Ana. Last night I studied a little and slept well.

lessons.culturalNote: Spanish tells stories in the past tense the way English does — once you have hablé and fue, anecdotes open up.

lessons.title: Making plans
lessons.objective: Talk about the near future the easy way — ir a plus the infinitive.
lessons.culturalNote: Spanish plans the near future with going-to, just like English — voy a viajar feels instantly familiar.

lessons.title: Weather and seasons
lessons.objective: Talk about the weather with hace sol, hace frío — and name the four seasons.
lessons.culturalNote: Spaniards discuss the weather with hacer — to make — as if the sky were cooking it up.

lessons.title: Telling the time
lessons.objective: Tell the time — Es la una, Son las tres y media — and ask ¿Qué hora es?
lessons.culturalNote: Spain runs famously late — dinner at ten is normal, so telling the time matters.

lessons.title: Months and dates
lessons.objective: Name the months and give dates the Spanish way — el 3 de mayo.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which line writes the date correctly?
legacyExercises.explanation: The day needs its el and the month its de: el 3 de mayo.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the sentence before you write it: my birthday is in June.
legacyExercises.explanation: For the month alone, en is enough: Mi cumpleaños es en junio.

legacyExercises.prompt: Months stay lowercase. Choose the correct line.
legacyExercises.explanation: Diciembre never takes a capital: La fiesta es en diciembre.
options: La fiesta es en el diciembre.

answers: Mi cumpleaños es el cinco de enero.
legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: my birthday is January 5th.
legacyExercises.explanation: El 5 de enero — day first: Mi cumpleaños es el cinco de enero.

answers: Hoy es el tres de mayo.
legacyExercises.prompt: Translate into Spanish: Today is May 3rd.
legacyExercises.explanation: Day with el, month with de: Hoy es el tres de mayo.

legacyExercises.prompt: The month is June, always lowercase. Fill the gap: El concierto es el 20 de ___.
legacyExercises.explanation: Lowercase, as always: El concierto es el 20 de junio.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the birthday note. When is the writer's birthday?
legacyExercises.explanation: The first sentence gives the date: el 5 de enero.
legacyExercises.passage: Mi cumpleaños es el 5 de enero. La fiesta es el 10 de enero en mi casa. Mi hermana cumple en junio. Mis padres cumplen en diciembre.
legacyExercises.translation: My birthday is January 5th. The party is January 10th at my house. My sister's birthday is in June. My parents' birthdays are in December.

lessons.culturalNote: Spanish months stay lowercase, even mid-sentence — mayo, never Mayo.

lessons.title: At the market
lessons.objective: Buy by quantity — un kilo de, una botella de — and point with este and esta.
lessons.culturalNote: Spanish markets sell by the kilo and the half-kilo; medio kilo is the everyday unit.

lessons.title: Free time and hobbies
lessons.objective: Say what you love doing — Me gusta leer, Me encanta nadar.
lessons.culturalNote: El fútbol is practically a religion in Spain; juego al fútbol will start conversations anywhere.

lessons.title: Health and the body
lessons.objective: Name body parts and say what hurts — Me duele la cabeza.
lessons.culturalNote: Spanish pharmacies are the first stop for minor ailments; the pharmacist advises before the doctor does.

lessons.title: At the pharmacy
lessons.objective: Ask for what you need at the pharmacy — Necesito algo para el dolor.
lessons.culturalNote: In Spain many medicines need no prescription — es sin receta is a phrase worth knowing.

lessons.title: Emergencies
lessons.objective: Handle emergencies — ¡Socorro!, Llame a una ambulancia, ¿Dónde está el hospital?

legacyExercises.prompt: Which line gives the formal command to call an ambulance?
legacyExercises.explanation: Llame is the formal command, and llamar needs its a: Llame a una ambulancia.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the question before you write it: where is the hospital?
legacyExercises.explanation: Dónde with its accent, está for location: ¿Dónde está el hospital?

legacyExercises.prompt: Emergencies use the formal command. Choose the correct cry.
legacyExercises.explanation: Llame is the usted command — Llamo would mean I call, which helps nobody.

answers: Llame a una ambulancia, por favor.
legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: call an ambulance, please.
legacyExercises.explanation: The command first, then a una ambulancia: Llame a una ambulancia, por favor.

legacyExercises.prompt: Translate into Spanish: I need help!
legacyExercises.explanation: Necesito ayuda, with the marks that frame it: ¡Necesito ayuda!

legacyExercises.prompt: This is the cry for help. Fill the gap: ¡___!
legacyExercises.explanation: ¡Socorro! is the cry for help.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the emergency. What does the woman call?
legacyExercises.explanation: The second sentence says it: llama a una ambulancia.
legacyExercises.passage: Hay una emergencia. Un hombre grita: ¡Socorro! Una mujer llama a una ambulancia. La ambulancia llega rápido. El hombre está bien.
legacyExercises.translation: There is an emergency. A man shouts: Help! A woman calls an ambulance. The ambulance arrives quickly. The man is fine.

lessons.culturalNote: 112 is the Europe-wide emergency number, and it works everywhere in Spain.

lessons.title: Invitations
lessons.objective: Invite, accept and decline — Te invito a cenar, ¡Claro que sí!, Lo siento, no puedo.
lessons.culturalNote: Spaniards often confirm plans at the last minute; no news before the party is usually good news.

lessons.title: Formar el pretérito
lessons.objective: Build the past tense: full -ar/-er/-ir endings and the big irregulars.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which ending marks the yo form of -ar verbs in the past?
legacyExercises.explanation: trabajé — the é is the I-did-it marker. trabajo is present (I work), trabaja is he/she present, trabajar is the untouched infinitive.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the yo past of comer: Yesterday I ate → Ayer ___ .
legacyExercises.explanation: -er/-ir verbs take -í for yo: comí. Keep the accent — comi without it is a spelling mistake, not a past tense.

legacyExercises.prompt: Estuvo enfermo ayer. Which verb is the rebel here?
legacyExercises.explanation: estuvo — estar's past ignores the -ar pattern completely (no *estó). enfermo is an adjective, ayer a time word, and fue isn't even in the sentence.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: We ate paella on Sunday.
legacyExercises.explanation: Comimos paella el domingo — verb first, then what, then when. The past verb carries the whole sentence.

legacyExercises.prompt: Translate into Spanish: He told me no.
legacyExercises.explanation: decir → dijo in the past — one of the rebels. Me dijo que no: told-me that no.

legacyExercises.prompt: Anoche ___ la tarea. (hacer, yo)
legacyExercises.explanation: hacer → hice. The yo past of hacer drops the pattern — memorize hice the way you memorized fue.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the day. What time did the narrator get home?
legacyExercises.explanation: Llegué a casa a las once — the last pretérito of the story, and your answer.
legacyExercises.passage: Ayer fue un día largo. Me levanté a las siete, desayuné café con tostadas y salí a trabajar. Por la tarde hablé con mi jefe y terminé el informe. Por la noche cené con amigos y llegué a casa a las once.
legacyExercises.translation: Yesterday was a long day. I got up at seven, had coffee with toast for breakfast and left for work. In the afternoon I spoke with my boss and finished the report. At night I had dinner with friends and got home at eleven.

lessons.culturalNote: In Spain the pretérito perfecto (he hablado) covers the recent past; across much of Latin America the simple pretérito (hablé) does that job too. Both are understood everywhere — pick one and stay consistent.

lessons.title: El imperfecto
lessons.objective: Use the imperfecto for habits, settings and background scenes.
lessons.culturalNote: Storytellers in Spanish love the imperfecto for scene-setting — novels open with era, había, llovía. Listen for it in any story and you will feel the scene slow down around you.

lessons.title: Pretérito o imperfecto
lessons.objective: Choose the right past: pretérito for events, imperfecto for background.
lessons.culturalNote: Spanish speakers mix both pasts in one breath — Hacía sol y de repente llovió. Mastering the switch is the moment your Spanish starts sounding natural instead of translated.

lessons.title: Contar el fin de semana
lessons.objective: Tell your weekend in the past: sequence words and past verbs.
lessons.culturalNote: ¿Qué hiciste el fin de semana? is the Monday-morning question everywhere in the Spanish-speaking world — offices, schools, bars. This lesson hands you the answer.

lessons.title: Formar el futuro
lessons.objective: Form the simple future: infinitive + endings, plus the rebel stems.

legacyExercises.prompt: How is the simple future formed?
legacyExercises.explanation: infinitive + endings: hablar + é = hablaré. -aba is the imperfecto; the infinitive stays whole — nothing is removed.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the yo future of comer.
legacyExercises.explanation: comer + é = comeré. Same ending for -ar, -er and -ir — the future doesn't care about verb groups.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which verb keeps a normal stem in the future?
legacyExercises.explanation: hablaré — hablar is regular. tener→tendré, poder→podré and decir→diré are three of the six rebel stems.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: Tomorrow I will speak with him.
legacyExercises.explanation: Mañana hablaré con él — when, what, with whom. The future verb carries the promise.

legacyExercises.prompt: Translate into Spanish: We will eat at two.
legacyExercises.explanation: comer + emos = comeremos. The nosotros ending is the only one with the stress on the ending's first syllable.

legacyExercises.prompt: El viernes ___ a cenar. (salir, nosotros)
legacyExercises.explanation: salir → saldr-: saldremos. The d sneaks in — one of the six rebels.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the week ahead. When will the narrator travel to Barcelona?
legacyExercises.explanation: el martes viajaré — the future verb plus its day. Plans wear dates.
legacyExercises.passage: La próxima semana será intensa. El lunes tendré una reunión importante y el martes viajaré a Barcelona. El miércoles haré una presentación y el jueves podré descansar. El viernes saldremos a cenar para celebrar.
legacyExercises.translation: Next week will be intense. On Monday I will have an important meeting and on Tuesday I will travel to Barcelona. On Wednesday I will give a presentation and on Thursday I will be able to rest. On Friday we will go out to dinner to celebrate.

lessons.culturalNote: In speech, many speakers prefer ir a + infinitive (voy a viajar) for personal plans — but the simple future owns predictions, promises and formal plans. Know both, and you will hear the difference in register.

lessons.title: Usos del futuro
lessons.objective: Use the future for promises, predictions and present guesses.
lessons.culturalNote: ¿Será verdad? — I wonder if it's true? The future of supposition softens questions into wonderings and is everywhere in conversation. It is also how weather forecasts speak: Mañana lloverá.

lessons.title: Planes e intenciones
lessons.objective: State plans with ir a + infinitive and wishes with querer.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which sentence states a decided plan?
legacyExercises.explanation: Voy a = decided and happening. quizá = maybe; estudiaba = used to; estudié = finished. Only ir a carries a live plan.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict: you (tú) are going to come → ___ a venir.
legacyExercises.explanation: ir gives vas for tú — vas a venir. The a is the bridge; the second verb never changes.

legacyExercises.prompt: Vamos a comprar una casa. Who is 'we'?
legacyExercises.explanation: vamos = we (nosotros) — the plan includes me. The ending -amos is the giveaway.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: I am going to learn Italian.
legacyExercises.explanation: Voy a aprender italiano — conjugated ir, then a, then the untouched infinitive. That order never changes.

legacyExercises.prompt: Translate into Spanish: We are going to travel in summer.
legacyExercises.explanation: Vamos a viajar — we-plan in four syllables. En verano pins down when.

legacyExercises.prompt: ___ a venir a la fiesta? (tú, are you going to…)
legacyExercises.explanation: ¿Vas a venir? — the invitation check. Vas, not *voy: the plan is theirs, not yours.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the life plan. Who is going to live with the narrator?
legacyExercises.explanation: Mi hermana va a venir a vivir conmigo — va a, the third-person plan.
legacyExercises.passage: El próximo año voy a cambiar mi vida. Voy a buscar un trabajo nuevo y voy a aprender italiano. Mi hermana va a venir a vivir conmigo y vamos a viajar juntas en verano. Son planes grandes, pero tengo la intención de cumplirlos.
legacyExercises.translation: Next year I am going to change my life. I am going to look for a new job and I am going to learn Italian. My sister is going to come live with me and we are going to travel together in summer. They are big plans, but I intend to keep them.

lessons.culturalNote: New Year's resolutions across the Spanish-speaking world start with Este año voy a… — say it out loud and the plan feels real. Voy a is also how friends make weekend plans on the spot.

lessons.title: El condicional
lessons.objective: Use the conditional for wishes, advice and polite requests.
lessons.culturalNote: ¿Podrías…? opens every polite request in Spanish — sharper than the imperative, warmer than a plain question. It is the single most useful verb form a traveler can own.

lessons.title: Cortesía: me gustaría, quisiera
lessons.objective: Ask politely: me gustaría, quisiera and the manners that open doors.
lessons.culturalNote: In Spain and Latin America a softened request gets a warmer answer — Quisiera is the traveler's magic word in every restaurant, shop and hotel. Pair it with por favor and perdona and you will never sound demanding.

lessons.title: Quiero que…: el subjuntivo
lessons.objective: Trigger the subjunctive with quiero que, necesito que, es importante que.

answers: a wish on someone else triggers the subjunctive
legacyExercises.prompt: Quiero que vengas. Why vengas and not vienes?
legacyExercises.explanation: a wish on someone else — quiero que flips the second verb into the subjunctive. Same subject would stay infinitive: Quiero venir.
options: a wish on someone else triggers the subjunctive

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the subjunctive: quiero que ___ (hablar, tú).
legacyExercises.explanation: hablo → hable → hables: drop the -o, add the opposite ending, then the tú -s. The recipe never changes.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which trigger needs the subjunctive?
legacyExercises.explanation: quiero que — wanting triggers it. creer, saber and es verdad keep the indicative: Creo que viene (fact, not wish).

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: I need you to help me.
legacyExercises.explanation: Necesito que me ayudes — the need, the que-bridge, then the subjunctive. Word order is mercifully simple.

legacyExercises.prompt: Translate into Spanish: It's important that you study. (tú)
legacyExercises.explanation: Es importante que estudies — the impersonal trigger works exactly like quiero que.

legacyExercises.prompt: Quiero que ___ a la fiesta. (venir, tú)
legacyExercises.explanation: Quiero que vengas — venir's subjunctive is irregular (veng-), but the trigger is perfectly regular.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the mother's rules. How many hours of sleep does she want?
legacyExercises.explanation: es importante que duermas ocho horas — the subjunctive duermas carries the mother's wish.
legacyExercises.passage: Mi madre siempre dice lo mismo: quiero que estudies, necesito que me ayudes en casa y es importante que duermas ocho horas. Yo quiero que me deje en paz, pero sé que tiene razón. Quiero que sea feliz, así que la ayudo.
legacyExercises.translation: My mother always says the same thing: I want you to study, I need you to help me at home and it's important that you sleep eight hours. I want her to leave me alone, but I know she's right. I want her to be happy, so I help her.

lessons.culturalNote: The subjunctive is the mood of wishes, doubts and feelings — the moment you use it, your Spanish stops sounding like a phrasebook and starts sounding like a person. Natives notice it instantly.

lessons.title: Que, quien, donde
lessons.objective: Link clauses with que, quien/quienes, donde, el que and lo que.
lessons.culturalNote: Relative clauses let you pack a whole story into one sentence — the difference between pointing at things and actually describing your world. Fluent speakers glue constantly; learners list.

lessons.title: Comparativos
lessons.objective: Compare with más/menos…que, tan…como, mejor/peor.

answers: Es tan alto como su hermano.
legacyExercises.prompt: Which sentence compares two things as equal?
legacyExercises.explanation: tan…como = as…as — equality. más/menos…que compare unequally; el más alto crowns him above all.
options: Es tan alto como su hermano.
Es más alto que su hermano.
Es menos alto que su hermano.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict: better → ___.
legacyExercises.explanation: mejor — bueno's rebel form. Never *más bueno; the rebel replaces the formula.

answers: before a number, que becomes de
legacyExercises.prompt: Más de tres personas. Why de and not que?
legacyExercises.explanation: before a number, que becomes de: más de tres, menos de diez. Numbers get their own preposition.
options: before a number, que becomes de

answers: Madrid es más grande que Sevilla.
legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: Madrid is bigger than Seville.
legacyExercises.explanation: Madrid es más grande que Sevilla — the formula in order: noun, es, más, adjective, que, rival.

answers: Mi piso es menos caro que el tuyo.
legacyExercises.prompt: Translate into Spanish: My flat is less expensive than yours.
legacyExercises.explanation: menos caro que — less follows the same formula as more. El tuyo = yours, no noun repeated.

legacyExercises.prompt: Es ___ alto como su hermano. (as…)
legacyExercises.explanation: tan…como — the equality pair. Tan opens it, como closes it.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the brothers. Who cooks better?
legacyExercises.explanation: cocino mejor que él — I cook better than him. Mejor settles the kitchen debate.
legacyExercises.passage: Mi hermano y yo somos muy diferentes. Él es más alto que yo y corre más rápido. Yo soy menos deportista, pero cocino mejor que él. Nuestra madre dice que somos tan tercos como nuestro padre. En el fondo, nos queremos más que a nadie.
legacyExercises.translation: My brother and I are very different. He is taller than me and runs faster. I am less sporty, but I cook better than him. Our mother says we are as stubborn as our father. Deep down, we love each other more than anyone.

lessons.culturalNote: Comparisons fuel friendly debate — ¿Cuál es mejor? starts conversations in every bar in Spain. Have an opinion, defend it with tan…como, and you are in.

lessons.title: Pronombres: lo, la, le
lessons.objective: Swap nouns for lo/la/le/les and combine them into se lo.
lessons.culturalNote: Pronouns are the oil of Spanish conversation — natives drop nouns constantly. Lo vi, se lo dije: short, fast, natural. Repeating the noun every time marks you as a beginner instantly.

lessons.title: Por y para
lessons.objective: Split por (cause, through) from para (purpose, deadline).

legacyExercises.prompt: Estudio para aprender. Para here marks…
legacyExercises.explanation: purpose — para aprender = in order to learn, the goal ahead. Causes and movement belong to por.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict: Thanks for your help → gracias ___ tu ayuda.
legacyExercises.explanation: gracias por — por looks back at what you're thankful for. The help already happened.

legacyExercises.prompt: Lo hice por ti. Por here means…
legacyExercises.explanation: because of you — por ti names the cause behind the action. The recipient reading (*for you as destination) would be para ti.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: It's for you.
legacyExercises.explanation: Es para ti — the recipient gets para. Three words, one direction: forward.

legacyExercises.prompt: Translate into Spanish: I need it for tomorrow.
legacyExercises.explanation: para mañana — the deadline reading of para. By tomorrow, not because of tomorrow.

legacyExercises.prompt: Paso ___ Madrid para ver a mi hermana. (through…)
legacyExercises.explanation: por Madrid = through Madrid — movement through space. Then para ver: the purpose of the stop.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the trip. When does the narrator return?
legacyExercises.explanation: Vuelvo el lunes por la noche — por la noche is por's time-of-day reading: in/during the night.
legacyExercises.passage: Mañana salgo de viaje por trabajo. Paso por Madrid para ver a mi hermana y después sigo para Barcelona. Llevo este regalo para ella y una carta para su jefe. Lo hago por cariño: para mí, la familia es lo primero. Vuelvo el lunes por la noche.
legacyExercises.translation: Tomorrow I leave on a work trip. I pass through Madrid to see my sister and then continue to Barcelona. I'm bringing this gift for her and a letter for her boss. I do it out of affection: for me, family comes first. I return Monday night.

lessons.culturalNote: Por vs para is the classic learner headache — but natives hear the logic instantly: por explains, para intends. Get the direction right (backward vs forward) and you are understood even when you hesitate.

lessons.title: Superlativos y el trabajo
lessons.objective: Crown the best with el más… and -ísimo; talk about work.

answers: Es el más alto de la clase.
legacyExercises.prompt: Which sentence is a superlative?
legacyExercises.explanation: Es el más alto de la clase — el más…de crowns him above all. más…que only compares two; tan…como declares equality.
options: Es el más alto de la clase.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the -ísimo form of bueno.
legacyExercises.explanation: bueno → buenísimo: drop the -o, weld on -ísimo. Extreme good, one word.

legacyExercises.prompt: La oficina es grandísima. Grandísima means…
legacyExercises.explanation: huge — -ísima cranks grande to the extreme. It's not a diminutive; it's a megaphone.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: I have an interview tomorrow.
legacyExercises.explanation: Tengo una entrevista mañana — have, what, when. The job hunt in four words.

legacyExercises.prompt: Translate into Spanish: My schedule is flexible.
legacyExercises.explanation: Mi horario es flexible — el horario, masculine. States of things wear ser.

legacyExercises.prompt: Mis compañeros son ___ más amables del mundo.
legacyExercises.explanation: los — the article must match compañeros (masculine plural). El más…de needs its article to agree.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the new job. How many days a week does the narrator work?
legacyExercises.explanation: trabajo cuatro días por semana — and calls the schedule buenísimo. The superlative earns its keep.
legacyExercises.passage: Mi trabajo nuevo es el mejor que he tenido. La oficina es grandísima y está en el centro. Mi jefe es exigente pero justo, y mis compañeros son los más amables del mundo. El sueldo no es altísimo, pero el horario es buenísimo: trabajo cuatro días por semana.
legacyExercises.translation: My new job is the best I've had. The office is huge and it's downtown. My boss is demanding but fair, and my colleagues are the kindest in the world. The salary isn't super high, but the schedule is great: I work four days a week.

lessons.culturalNote: Job interviews in Spanish love superlatives — Soy el más adecuado para el puesto. Confidence, grammatically delivered, in the language employers actually hear.

lessons.title: Misión: en el hotel
lessons.objective: Check into a hotel: greet, confirm your booking, ask about breakfast, report a problem.

lessons.title: Tecnología
lessons.objective: Handle tech in Spanish: passwords, screens, sending and downloading.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which sentence asks for the wifi password?
legacyExercises.explanation: ¿Cuál es…? asks which one it is — the password itself. Dónde asks where, qué asks what it is, cuánto asks the price.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the yo present of enviar: te ___ un mensaje.
legacyExercises.explanation: enviar is regular: envío. Tech verbs rarely surprise you — learn the noun, the verb behaves.

legacyExercises.prompt: La contraseña del wifi. Del = …
legacyExercises.explanation: de + el — the mandatory contraction. *De el wifi is always wrong, in every register.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: Download the app.
legacyExercises.explanation: Descarga la aplicación — command, then what. Imperatives lead with the verb.

legacyExercises.prompt: Translate into Spanish: The screen is broken.
legacyExercises.explanation: La pantalla está rota — broken states wear estar, not ser. La pantalla is feminine: rota, not roto.

legacyExercises.prompt: Te ___ el documento. (enviar, yo)
legacyExercises.explanation: Te envío — the indirect pronoun te rides before the verb: I send it to you.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the phone saga. What did the technician say was fine?
legacyExercises.explanation: la batería está bien — está, because it's a state. The fix was the update, not the battery.
legacyExercises.passage: Ayer mi móvil dejó de funcionar. La pantalla se quedó en negro y no encendía. Fui a una tienda y el técnico me dijo: la batería está bien, pero necesitas actualizar el sistema. Descargué la actualización, encendí el móvil y funcionó. Ahora envío mensajes sin problema.
legacyExercises.translation: Yesterday my phone stopped working. The screen went black and wouldn't turn on. I went to a shop and the technician told me: the battery is fine, but you need to update the system. I downloaded the update, turned on the phone and it worked. Now I send messages without a problem.

lessons.culturalNote: ¿Tienes wifi? is the modern traveler's first question — la contraseña is the second. Tech Spanish borrows freely (el wifi, el email), so the nouns are the easy part; the verbs do the work.

lessons.title: El tren de las siete
lessons.objective: Tell a connected story of a delayed journey with primero, luego, después and al final — pretérito for what happened, imperfecto for the scene.
lessons.culturalNote: Spanish story-tellers switch tenses inside one story: the pretérito reports the beats (hubo un problema), the imperfecto holds the scene (había mucha gente).

answers: Hubo un problema en las vías.
legacyExercises.prompt: Which sentence reports a finished event, not a scene?
legacyExercises.explanation: Hubo is the pretérito of haber — an event that happened once. Había, eran and hacía paint the scene instead.
options: Hubo un problema en las vías.
Había mucha gente en el andén.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the pretérito of haber for the story's event: ___ un problema en las vías.
legacyExercises.explanation: Hubo — the event. Había would paint the scene instead.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which word opens the story's order, the first beat?
legacyExercises.explanation: Primero opens the chain; luego and después continue it, and al final closes it.

legacyExercises.prompt: ___ mucha gente en la estación. (haber)
legacyExercises.explanation: Había paints the scene; hubo would snap an event.

legacyExercises.prompt: Translate into Spanish: First I went to the station.
legacyExercises.explanation: Primero + fui — the first event of the story's chain.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the story. What time did the narrator and her sister finally reach their aunt and uncle's house?
legacyExercises.explanation: Al final llegamos a casa de nuestros tíos a las diez — the story closes at ten.
legacyExercises.passage: Primero fui a la estación con mi hermana. Eran las seis y media y había mucha gente esperando. Luego vimos que el tren de las siete llevaba retraso: hubo un problema en las vías. Al final llegamos a casa de nuestros tíos a las diez.
legacyExercises.translation: First I went to the station with my sister. It was half past six and lots of people were waiting. Then we saw that the seven o'clock train was delayed: there was a problem on the tracks. In the end we reached our aunt and uncle's house at ten.

legacyExercises.prompt: From memory: the marker that closes the story after the delay.
legacyExercises.explanation: Al final — the closing marker of the chain.

lessons.title: El vuelo cancelado
lessons.objective: Read a news report about a cancelled flight: extract the main point and two supporting details, and follow the conditional of hypothesis (sería, habría).
lessons.culturalNote: Spanish news softens announced plans with the conditional — reprogramaría, sería — where English would often use would.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which action does the airline offer after the cancellation?
legacyExercises.explanation: Reprogramar — to rebook — is the airline's offer in the report.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the conditional of reprogramar in the report: la compañía dijo que ___ los vuelos.
legacyExercises.explanation: Reprogramaría — the conditional -ría reports the announced plan.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which pair is the conditional of hypothesis?
legacyExercises.explanation: Sería, habría — the might-be pair of the report.

legacyExercises.prompt: Según la portavoz, ___ posible salir el domingo. (ser)
legacyExercises.explanation: Sería — the conditional, for the spokesperson's cautious claim.

answers: Habría que confirmar el nuevo horario.
legacyExercises.prompt: Translate into Spanish: It would be necessary to confirm the new schedule.
legacyExercises.explanation: Habría que + infinitive: it would be necessary to…

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the report. What must passengers do before midday?
legacyExercises.explanation: Revisar el correo electrónico y aceptar la nueva reserva — the report's deadline instruction.
legacyExercises.passage: La compañía Aerolínea Costa canceló el vuelo CO-417 por el mal tiempo. Dijo que reprogramaría los vuelos sin coste adicional. Los viajeros deben revisar el correo electrónico y aceptar la nueva reserva antes de las doce.
legacyExercises.translation: Airline Aerolínea Costa cancelled flight CO-417 because of the bad weather. It said it would rebook the flights free of charge. Travellers must check their email and accept the new booking before midday.

legacyExercises.prompt: From memory: the company's offer, in the conditional — it would rebook the flights.
legacyExercises.explanation: Reprogramaría los vuelos — the reported plan in the conditional.

lessons.title: En el aeropuerto
lessons.objective: Follow a spoken airport exchange: catch the gist and two details, and ask politely for a repeat when an announcement passes you by.
lessons.culturalNote: Over airport speakers Spanish clocks stay precise: a las siete y cuarto, la puerta doce — the numbers do the work.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which line politely interrupts someone to ask again?
legacyExercises.explanation: Perdone + ¿puede repetir? — the courteous request for a repeat.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the form of faltar with one hour: ___ una hora para el vuelo.
legacyExercises.explanation: Falta — singular with una hora; the time still to go.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which time is the clear new boarding time?
legacyExercises.explanation: A las siete y cuarto — the exact time in the exchange.

legacyExercises.prompt: Perdone, ¿puede ___ el aviso, por favor?
legacyExercises.explanation: Repetir — the infinitive after puede.

answers: La nueva hora de embarque es a las siete y cuarto.
legacyExercises.prompt: Translate into Spanish: The new boarding time is a quarter past seven.
legacyExercises.explanation: La nueva hora de embarque es a las siete y cuarto.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the exchange. Which gate does the flight board from?
legacyExercises.explanation: La puerta número doce — the same gate, number twelve.
legacyExercises.passage: — El vuelo a Sevilla lleva retraso: falta una hora para la nueva salida. El nuevo embarque es a las siete y cuarto. — ¿Y la puerta es la misma? — Sí, la número doce.
legacyExercises.translation: — The flight to Seville is delayed: there is an hour before the new departure. The new boarding is at a quarter past seven. — And is the gate the same? — Yes, number twelve.

legacyExercises.prompt: From memory: the polite interruption that asks for a repeat.
legacyExercises.explanation: Perdone, ¿puede repetir? — the courteous opener of the exchange.

lessons.title: Reprogramar el viaje
lessons.objective: Hold a courteous exchange with a travel agent: make a soft request, give a reason with porque, and confirm the new plan.
lessons.culturalNote: At a Spanish service counter the polite conditional does the asking: me gustaría, podría, quería — followed by a full sentence of reason with porque.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which request sounds most courteous at an airline counter?
legacyExercises.explanation: Me gustaría cambiar mi vuelo — the conditional keeps the request courteous.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the polite frame: Me ___ cambiar mi billete. (gustar)
legacyExercises.explanation: Gustaría — the conditional of gustar, the courteous frame.

answers: Lo quiero cambiar porque tengo una reunión.
legacyExercises.prompt: Which sentence gives the reason with porque?
legacyExercises.explanation: Porque tengo una reunión — porque introduces the reason as a full sentence.
options: Lo quiero cambiar porque tengo una reunión.
Lo quiero cambiar por la mañana.

legacyExercises.prompt: Me ___ cambiar mi billete al lunes. (gustar)
legacyExercises.explanation: Gustaría — the courteous conditional.

answers: Quería preguntar por el vuelo de mañana.
legacyExercises.prompt: Translate into Spanish: I wanted to ask about tomorrow's flight.
legacyExercises.explanation: Quería preguntar por el vuelo de mañana — the polite imperfect opener.

answers: Porque tiene una reunión importante el lunes.
legacyExercises.prompt: Read the exchange. Why does the traveller want to change the flight?
legacyExercises.explanation: Porque tiene una reunión importante el lunes — the reason stated with porque.
legacyExercises.passage: — Buenas tardes. Me gustaría cambiar mi vuelo a Valencia. — Claro. ¿Por qué lo quiere cambiar? — Porque tengo una reunión importante el lunes. — ¿Le importaría viajar el martes por la mañana? — El martes me va bien, gracias.
legacyExercises.translation: — Good afternoon. I would like to change my flight to Valencia. — Of course. Why do you want to change it? — Because I have an important meeting on Monday. — Would you mind travelling on Tuesday morning? — Tuesday works for me, thank you.

legacyExercises.prompt: From memory: ask the agent for another date, courteously.
legacyExercises.explanation: ¿Podría darme otra fecha? — the courteous conditional request.

lessons.title: Cuenta tu viaje
lessons.objective: Write a short connected account of a disrupted trip: order markers, past verbs and one porque reason.
lessons.culturalNote: Written Spanish keeps the story-telling skeleton visible: primero, luego, después, al final keep the reader oriented beat by beat.

answers: Primero perdimos el tren de las nueve.
legacyExercises.prompt: Which sentence writes a complete story beat with an order marker?
legacyExercises.explanation: Primero perdimos el tren — a marker plus a finished event.
options: Primero perdimos el tren de las nueve.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the connector that continues the chain: ___ esperamos en la estación.
legacyExercises.explanation: Luego (or después) — then; the next beat of the story.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which connector gives the reason?
legacyExercises.explanation: Porque — the reason connector.

legacyExercises.prompt: Perdimos el tren ___ salimos tarde de casa. (reason)
legacyExercises.explanation: Porque — one word, the reason connector.

answers: Al final llegamos al hotel a medianoche.
legacyExercises.prompt: Translate into Spanish: In the end we reached the hotel at midnight.
legacyExercises.explanation: Al final llegamos al hotel a medianoche — the closing beat.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the story. Why did the travellers miss the nine o'clock train?
legacyExercises.explanation: Porque el despertador no sonó — the alarm clock was the cause.
legacyExercises.passage: El viaje a la costa fue un desastre. Primero salimos tarde de casa porque el despertador no sonó. Luego perdimos el tren de las nueve y esperamos dos horas en la estación. Al final llegamos al hotel a medianoche.
legacyExercises.translation: The trip to the coast was a disaster. First we left home late because the alarm clock did not ring. Then we missed the nine o'clock train and waited two hours at the station. In the end we reached the hotel at midnight.

legacyExercises.prompt: From memory: write the closing beat — we finally arrived at the hotel.
legacyExercises.explanation: Al final llegamos al hotel — the written ending.

lessons.title: La reclamación
lessons.objective: Present a compensation claim at the airline's claims desk: report what you were told, state the consequence, and close with a polite request.
lessons.culturalNote: At a Spanish service desk the claim stays courteous: quisiera reclamar opens it, and me dijeron que carries what the company told you.

lessons.title: El año que viene
lessons.objective: State your work and study plans for next year: ir a for decided plans, the present for fixed schedules, and the future simple for predictions.
lessons.culturalNote: Spanish plans split three ways: ir a for what you have decided, the present for fixed dates on the calendar, and the future simple for what will probably come.

answers: Voy a estudiar diseño el año que viene.
legacyExercises.prompt: Which sentence reports a plan you have decided?
legacyExercises.explanation: Voy a estudiar — ir a + infinitive for the decided plan.
options: Voy a estudiar diseño el año que viene.

errors.explanation: The ir a plan keeps its a: voy a.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the decided-plan frame: ___ a estudiar diseño el año que viene.
legacyExercises.explanation: Voy a — ir a + infinitive for the decided plan.

answers: Las clases de inglés empiezan a las nueve.
legacyExercises.prompt: Which tense states a fixed schedule?
legacyExercises.explanation: The present — empiezan a las nueve.
options: Las clases de inglés empiezan a las nueve.
Las clases de inglés empezarán a las nueve.
Voy a empezar las clases de inglés.

legacyExercises.prompt: El curso de diseño ___ en octubre. (empezar)
legacyExercises.explanation: Empieza — the present for the fixed date.

answers: Voy a solicitar el puesto porque necesito más experiencia.
legacyExercises.prompt: Translate into Spanish: I'm going to apply for the job because I need more experience.
legacyExercises.explanation: Voy a solicitar el puesto porque necesito más experiencia — the plan and its porque reason.

answers: Porque quiere trabajar en un hospital.
legacyExercises.prompt: Read the text. Why is Ana going to study nursing?
legacyExercises.explanation: Porque quiere trabajar en un hospital — her porque reason.
legacyExercises.passage: Ana termina el instituto en junio. El año que viene va a estudiar enfermería en Salamanca porque quiere trabajar en un hospital. Las clases empiezan en septiembre, pero antes participa en un curso de verano. Después trabajará en el hospital de su ciudad, si todo va bien.
legacyExercises.translation: Ana finishes school in June. Next year she's going to study nursing in Salamanca because she wants to work in a hospital. The classes start in September, but before that she takes part in a summer course. Afterwards she'll work in her city's hospital, if all goes well.

answers: El año que viene voy a estudiar enfermería.
legacyExercises.prompt: From memory: the decided plan for next year, with ir a.
legacyExercises.explanation: El año que viene voy a estudiar enfermería.

lessons.title: La llamada de la oferta
lessons.objective: Follow a job-offer call: catch the offer, the salary and the start date, and repeat politely when the line blurs.
lessons.culturalNote: On a Spanish job call the routine phrases keep it friendly: a ver, ¿me oyes? checks the line, and podría + infinitive softens the offer.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which phrase keeps a phone call going when the line is unclear?
legacyExercises.explanation: A ver, ¿me oyes? — the courteous line-check.

errors.explanation: The offer keeps its courtesy in the conditional: podría.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the conditional of empezar in the offer: ___ empezar el lunes.
legacyExercises.explanation: Podría — the conditional softens the offer.

answers: Estoy de prácticas en la agencia.
legacyExercises.prompt: Which phrase names temporary work with estar de?
legacyExercises.explanation: Estoy de becaria — estar de for the temporary role.
options: Estoy de prácticas en la agencia.
Soy la directora de la agencia.

legacyExercises.prompt: Gano ___ ochocientos euros al mes. (the spoken number)
legacyExercises.explanation: Mil — the spoken number: mil ochocientos.

answers: El sueldo es de mil ochocientos euros.
legacyExercises.prompt: Translate into Spanish: The salary is one thousand eight hundred euros.
legacyExercises.explanation: El sueldo es de mil ochocientos euros — the spoken salary figure.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the exchange. What does the caller offer about Monday?
legacyExercises.explanation: Podría empezar el lunes — the conditional offer.
legacyExercises.passage: — A ver, ¿me oyes bien? — Sí, ahora te oigo. — Le llamo por la oferta de la agencia. ¿Podría empezar el lunes? El sueldo es de mil ochocientos euros al mes. — ¿Y el horario? — Flexible: empezamos a las nueve.
legacyExercises.translation: — Hello, can you hear me well? — Yes, I hear you now. — I'm calling you about the agency's offer. Could I start on Monday? The salary is one thousand eight hundred euros a month. — And the timetable? — Flexible: we start at nine.

legacyExercises.prompt: From memory: the conditional offer — could start on Monday.
legacyExercises.explanation: Podría empezar el lunes.

lessons.title: Una entrevista
lessons.objective: Read a candidate's interview article: extract the main point and two supporting details, and follow the comparatives and porque reasons.
lessons.culturalNote: An interview write-up weighs options: más… que compares, el más crowns the best, and porque explains the choice.

answers: Este puesto es más estable que el otro.
legacyExercises.prompt: Which sentence weighs two options with más… que?
legacyExercises.explanation: Más… que — the unequal comparison.
options: Este puesto es más estable que el otro.
Este puesto es el más estable de todos.
Este puesto es tan estable como el otro.

errors.explanation: The comparative link is que: más interesante que el otro.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the comparative link: este puesto es más interesante ___ el otro.
legacyExercises.explanation: Que — the comparative link.

answers: La persona con quien hablé me ayudó.
legacyExercises.prompt: Which relative clause names a person correctly?
legacyExercises.explanation: Quien stays personal: la persona con quien hablé.
options: La persona con quien hablé me ayudó.
La oficina quien visité es moderna.
El informe quien leí fue largo.
La ciudad quien visitamos es grande.

legacyExercises.prompt: Este puesto paga ___ que el otro. (the comparative word)
legacyExercises.explanation: Más — the comparative word with its accent.

answers: La empresa que la contrató es la más grande de la ciudad.
legacyExercises.prompt: Translate into Spanish: The company that hired her is the biggest in the city.
legacyExercises.explanation: La empresa que la contrató es la más grande de la ciudad.

answers: Porque el equipo es pequeño y el jefe cercano.
legacyExercises.prompt: Read the article. Why does Valeria prefer the agency?
legacyExercises.explanation: Porque el equipo es pequeño y el jefe cercano — her reason.
legacyExercises.passage: Valeria busca su primer contrato tras seis meses de becaria. La editorial paga más, pero el puesto es más rutinario. Prefiere la agencia porque el equipo es pequeño y el jefe, con quien habló dos veces, le parece cercano. Los expertos recuerdan que la formación y el ambiente cuentan tanto como el dinero.
legacyExercises.translation: Valeria is looking for her first contract after six months as an intern. The publishing house pays more, but the post is more routine. She prefers the agency because the team is small and the boss, whom she spoke with twice, seems close. Experts remind us that training and atmosphere count as much as money.

legacyExercises.prompt: From memory: the relative that links the company.
legacyExercises.explanation: La empresa que la contrató — que for the company.

lessons.title: ¿Cuál elijo?
lessons.objective: Negotiate a choice between two job offers: weigh them with comparatives, give soft advice with deberías, and give reasons with porque.
lessons.culturalNote: Soft advice in Spanish uses the conditional: deberías keeps the friendship, debes gives an order.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which line gives soft advice?
legacyExercises.explanation: Deberías — the soft-advice conditional.

errors.explanation: Advice softens in the conditional: deberías.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the advice frame: ___ pedir más información.
legacyExercises.explanation: Deberías — the soft-advice conditional.

answers: Prefiero la agencia porque el equipo es pequeño.
legacyExercises.prompt: Which clause gives the reason with porque?
legacyExercises.explanation: Porque + the reason sentence.
options: Prefiero la agencia porque el equipo es pequeño.
Prefiero la agencia por la tarde.

legacyExercises.prompt: Deberías ___ (comparar) las dos ofertas antes de decidir.
legacyExercises.explanation: Comparar — the infinitive after deberías.

answers: Este puesto paga más que el otro.
legacyExercises.prompt: Translate into Spanish: This job pays more than the other one.
legacyExercises.explanation: Este puesto paga más que el otro.

answers: Porque es más pequeña, pero más cercana.
legacyExercises.prompt: Read the exchange. Why does the friend suggest the agency?
legacyExercises.explanation: Porque es más pequeña, pero más cercana.
legacyExercises.passage: — He recibido dos ofertas y no sé cuál elegir. — ¿Y qué te importa más? — La formación, porque quiero aprender. — Entonces la agencia es mejor para ti: es más pequeña, pero más cercana.
legacyExercises.translation: — I've received two offers and I don't know which to choose. — And what matters most to you? — The training, because I want to learn. — Then the agency is better for you: it's smaller, but closer.

legacyExercises.prompt: From memory: soft advice about the two offers.
legacyExercises.explanation: Deberías comparar las dos ofertas.

lessons.title: Tu plan de estudios
lessons.objective: Write a short study or work plan: ir a or the future, sequence markers, and at least one porque reason.
lessons.culturalNote: A written plan shows its shape: sequence markers first, verbs in ir a or the future, and a porque reason to close.

answers: Primero voy a terminar el curso.
legacyExercises.prompt: Which sentence opens a written plan with a marker?
legacyExercises.explanation: Primero voy a terminar el curso — a marker plus a step.
options: Primero voy a terminar el curso.

errors.explanation: Luego continues the plan; the first step opens with primero.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the first-step frame: ___ voy a terminar el curso.
legacyExercises.explanation: Primero — the opening marker.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which connector pairs the plan with its porque reason?
legacyExercises.explanation: Porque — the reason connector.

legacyExercises.prompt: Más tarde ___ (solicitar, yo) la beca, cuando termine el curso.
legacyExercises.explanation: Solicitaré — the future for the later step.

answers: Al final trabajaré en Madrid porque allí hay más oportunidades.
legacyExercises.prompt: Translate into Spanish: In the end I'll work in Madrid because there are more opportunities there.
legacyExercises.explanation: Al final trabajaré en Madrid porque allí hay más oportunidades.

answers: Porque le encanta el diseño publicitario.
legacyExercises.prompt: Read the plan. Why does the writer look for agency work?
legacyExercises.explanation: Porque le encanta el diseño publicitario — the porque reason.
legacyExercises.passage: Mi plan para el año que viene es claro. Primero voy a terminar el curso de diseño gráfico. Luego solicitaré una beca en el centro de estudios de Valencia. Al final buscaré trabajo en una agencia porque me encanta el diseño publicitario.
legacyExercises.translation: My plan for next year is clear. First I'm going to finish the graphic design course. Afterwards I'll apply for a scholarship at the study centre in Valencia. In the end I'll look for work at an agency because I love advertising design.

answers: Al final buscaré trabajo en una agencia.
legacyExercises.prompt: From memory: the closing step — look for agency work.
legacyExercises.explanation: Al final buscaré trabajo en una agencia.

lessons.title: La entrevista
lessons.objective: Take part in a mock job interview: introduce yourself, state your experience, make a polite request, and close courteously.
lessons.culturalNote: A Spanish interview opens with names and places: me llamo…, soy de…, llevo…; espero que takes the subjunctive.

lessons.title: Me gusta porque…
lessons.objective: Explain a preference with gustar or encantar plus a porque reason, and keep porque, por qué and por que apart in writing.
lessons.culturalNote: Tastes in Spanish turn the sentence round: the thing liked does the agreeing (me gusta el cine), and porque — one word, no accent — gives the reason.

answers: Me gusta el cine porque las historias me emocionan.
legacyExercises.prompt: Which sentence explains a taste with gustar and a porque reason?
legacyExercises.explanation: Me gusta el cine porque las historias me emocionan — gustar plus porque.
options: Me gusta el cine porque las historias me emocionan.
Me gusta el cine por la tarde.

errors.explanation: Por joins a noun; porque introduces the reason sentence.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the reason link: me gusta el museo ___ está tranquilo.
legacyExercises.explanation: Porque — the reason sentence.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which sentence asks the reason with the accent?
legacyExercises.explanation: ¿Por qué no vienes al concierto? — por qué with the accent.
options: Por que no vienes al concierto.

errors.explanation: Las películas is plural: gustan.

legacyExercises.prompt: A Laura ___ (gustar) las películas de aventuras.
legacyExercises.explanation: Gustan — the plural taste.

answers: Me gustan los conciertos porque la música es en directo.
legacyExercises.prompt: Translate into Spanish: I like concerts because the music is live.
legacyExercises.explanation: Me gustan los conciertos porque la música es en directo.

answers: Porque es lo único que aceptan los dos.

errors.explanation: That is Leo's objection, not the reason for the exhibition.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the text. Why do Sara and Leo go to the exhibition?
legacyExercises.explanation: Porque es lo único que aceptan los dos — the reason for the exhibition.
legacyExercises.passage: A Sara le gusta el cine porque las historias le emocionan. A Leo le gustan más los conciertos porque le encanta la música en directo. El sábado no se ponen de acuerdo: «¿Por qué no vamos al cine?», pregunta Sara. «Porque el cine está lejos», responde Leo. Al final van a la exposición de fotos porque es lo único que aceptan los dos.
legacyExercises.translation: Sara likes the cinema because the stories move her. Leo prefers concerts because he loves live music. On Saturday they cannot agree: 'Why don't we go to the cinema?' asks Sara. 'Because the cinema is far away,' replies Leo. In the end they go to the photography exhibition because it is the only thing they both accept.

answers: Me gusta el cine porque las historias me emocionan.
legacyExercises.prompt: From memory: the dative taste with porque.
legacyExercises.explanation: Me gusta el cine porque las historias me emocionan.

lessons.title: La llamada del cumpleaños
lessons.objective: Follow a birthday-planning call: catch the agreed plan and two details, and recognise the invitation frames in speech.
lessons.culturalNote: On a Spanish planning call the routine frames keep it warm: ¿te apetece…? proposes, claro que sí accepts, and quedamos en fixes the place.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which line proposes the plan with apetecer?
legacyExercises.explanation: ¿Te apetece venir a la fiesta? — the apetecer proposal.
options: Tienes que venir a la fiesta.
Ven a la fiesta o me enfado.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the accept frame: — ¿Te apetece venir? — Claro ___, gracias.
legacyExercises.explanation: Claro que sí — the warm accept.

answers: Quedamos en la plaza a las ocho.
legacyExercises.prompt: Which line fixes the meeting place with quedamos en?
legacyExercises.explanation: Quedamos en la plaza a las ocho — the meeting fixed.
options: Quedamos en la plaza a las ocho.
Quedamos la plaza a las ocho.
Somos en la plaza a las ocho.
Vamos de la plaza a las ocho.

errors.explanation: Nosotros takes celebramos.

legacyExercises.prompt: El sábado ___ (celebrar, nosotros) el cumpleaños de Andrés.
legacyExercises.explanation: Celebramos — the group's plan.

answers: Vamos a celebrarlo en la pizzería porque le encanta la pizza.
legacyExercises.prompt: Translate into Spanish: We're going to celebrate it in the pizzeria because he loves pizza.
legacyExercises.explanation: Vamos a celebrarlo en la pizzería porque le encanta la pizza.

answers: Quedan a las ocho en la plaza.

errors.explanation: The pizzeria is the second stop; the meeting place comes first.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the exchange. Where do they agree to meet?
legacyExercises.explanation: Quedan a las ocho en la plaza — the meeting place in the call.
legacyExercises.passage: — ¿Te apetece venir al cumpleaños de Andrés el sábado? — ¡Claro que sí! ¿Dónde quedamos? — Quedamos a las ocho en la plaza y luego vamos a la pizzería. — Perfecto. ¿Ponemos algo para el regalo? — Buena idea: un libro de fotografía, porque a Andrés le encanta.
legacyExercises.translation: — Do you fancy coming to Andrés's birthday on Saturday? — Of course! Where shall we meet? — We'll meet at eight in the square and then go to the pizzeria. — Perfect. Shall we put something in for the gift? — Good idea: a photography book, because Andrés loves it.

answers: Quedamos en la plaza a las ocho.
legacyExercises.prompt: From memory: the meeting frame — meet at the square at eight.
legacyExercises.explanation: Quedamos en la plaza a las ocho.

lessons.title: El aniversario
lessons.objective: Read a message-thread deliberation: extract the main point and two supporting details, and follow the conditional invitation and para + purpose.
lessons.culturalNote: A Spanish group plan mixes courtesy and aim: ¿te gustaría…? invites, para points forward, por names the occasion.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which line makes the invitation with the conditional?
legacyExercises.explanation: ¿Te gustaría organizar una cena? — the conditional invitation.

errors.explanation: Purpose takes para: para regalar.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the purpose link: compramos flores ___ regalar.
legacyExercises.explanation: Para — purpose: para regalar.

answers: Celebramos la cena por su aniversario.
legacyExercises.prompt: Which sentence names the occasion with por?
legacyExercises.explanation: Celebramos la cena por su aniversario — por for the occasion.
options: Celebramos la cena por su aniversario.
Celebramos la cena para su aniversario.
Celebramos la cena con su aniversario.
Celebramos la cena sin su aniversario.

errors.explanation: After gustaría the verb stays an infinitive: venir.

legacyExercises.prompt: ¿Te gustaría ___ (venir) a la cena del sábado?
legacyExercises.explanation: Venir — the infinitive after gustaría.

answers: ¿Te gustaría venir a la cena por su aniversario?
legacyExercises.prompt: Translate into Spanish: Would you like to come to the dinner for their anniversary?
legacyExercises.explanation: ¿Te gustaría venir a la cena por su aniversario?

answers: Porque la pareja prefiere la tranquilidad de casa.

errors.explanation: Leo's proposal is the idea they leave behind.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the thread. Why does the group choose the dinner at home?
legacyExercises.explanation: Porque la pareja prefiere la tranquilidad de casa.
legacyExercises.passage: Sara escribe al grupo: «¿Te gustaría organizar una cena por el aniversario de mis padres?». Leo propone un restaurante, pero Ana recuerda que la pareja prefiere la tranquilidad de casa. Por eso cenan en casa de Sara: cada uno aporta un plato. Para el regalo compran un libro de fotos y flores para regalar.
legacyExercises.translation: Sara writes to the group: "Would you like to organise a dinner for my parents' anniversary?" Leo proposes a restaurant, but Ana remembers the couple prefers the calm of home. So they eat at Sara's house: each person brings a dish. For the gift they buy a photo book and flowers to give.

legacyExercises.prompt: From memory: the purpose frame — flowers to give as a gift.
legacyExercises.explanation: Flores para regalar.

lessons.title: ¿Quedamos?
lessons.objective: Repair a misunderstanding and agree on a plan: propose with vamos a or quedamos en, ask with ¿qué te parece?, and accept or decline gracefully.
lessons.culturalNote: Plans are agreed, not announced: ¿qué te parece? asks, lo siento, no puedo declines without offence, and quedamos en seals it.

answers: ¿Qué te parece si vamos al cine?
legacyExercises.prompt: Which line asks the other's opinion with parecer?
legacyExercises.explanation: ¿Qué te parece si vamos al cine? — the opinion frame.
options: ¿Qué te parece si vamos al cine?

errors.explanation: Vamos a states the action; quedamos en fixes the place.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the meeting frame: ___ en la plaza a las ocho.
legacyExercises.explanation: Quedamos — the meeting frame.

answers: Claro que sí, me encanta la idea.
legacyExercises.prompt: Which line accepts the plan warmly?
legacyExercises.explanation: Claro que sí, me encanta la idea — the warm accept.
options: Claro que sí, me encanta la idea.
Puede que sí, no sé todavía.

errors.explanation: After voy a the verb stays an infinitive: proponer.

legacyExercises.prompt: Voy a ___ (proponer) una cena para el sábado.
legacyExercises.explanation: Proponer — the infinitive after voy a.

answers: Lo siento, no puedo venir el sábado.
legacyExercises.prompt: Translate into Spanish: I'm sorry, I can't come on Saturday.
legacyExercises.explanation: Lo siento, no puedo venir el sábado.

answers: Porque trabaja hasta tarde el sábado.

legacyExercises.explanation: Porque trabaja hasta tarde el sábado.

legacyExercises.translation: — What do you think about celebrating the dinner on Saturday? — I'm sorry, I can't on Saturday: I work late. — And Sunday? — Sunday suits me very well. We'll meet at your house at nine.

answers: Quedamos en tu casa a las nueve.
legacyExercises.prompt: From memory: the meeting frame — meet at your house at nine.
legacyExercises.explanation: Quedamos en tu casa a las nueve.

lessons.title: Tu decisión
lessons.objective: Write a short message justifying a social choice with a porque reason.
lessons.culturalNote: A written decision shows its shape: the choice first, the porque reason, and the plan to close.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which sentence opens a decision with a preference?
legacyExercises.explanation: Prefiero la cena en casa — the preference opener.

errors.explanation: The reason is one word without an accent: porque.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the reason link: prefiero el parque ___ es más tranquilo.
legacyExercises.explanation: Porque — the reason sentence.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which line asks the reason with por qué?
legacyExercises.explanation: ¿Por qué prefieres el parque? — por qué with the accent.
options: Por que no voy al parque.

errors.explanation: The polite wish is the conditional: me gustaría.

legacyExercises.prompt: Me ___ (gustar) celebrar mi cumpleaños en el parque.
legacyExercises.explanation: Gustaría — the polite wish in the conditional.

answers: Me gustaría celebrarlo en casa porque es más acogedor.

legacyExercises.explanation: Me gustaría celebrarlo en casa porque es más acogedor.

answers: Porque el restaurante es muy caro y el parque es tranquilo.

errors.explanation: The invitation is how the plan starts; the park has another reason.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the decision. Why does the writer choose the park?
legacyExercises.explanation: Porque el restaurante es muy caro y el parque es tranquilo.

Invito a mis amigos con un mensaje claro: «¿Qué os parece si quedamos en la fuente a las seis?». Al final llevamos la comida y la sorpresa, y no gastamos demasiado.
legacyExercises.translation: My decision for my birthday is simple. I prefer to celebrate it in the park because the restaurant is very expensive and the park is quiet. I invite my friends with a clear message: "What do you think about meeting at the fountain at six?" In the end we bring the food and the surprise, and we do not spend too much.

answers: Me gustaría celebrarlo en el parque.
legacyExercises.prompt: From memory: the polite wish frame — celebrate it in the park.
legacyExercises.explanation: Me gustaría celebrarlo en el parque.

lessons.title: El regalo del grupo
lessons.objective: Organise a group gift in a chat and a shop run: propose, name the occasion with por, the aim with para, and handle the se lo form lightly.
lessons.culturalNote: Por names the occasion, para the aim — and two pronouns line up as se lo, never le lo.

checkpoints.title: First steps in Spanish
checkpoints.introduction: A short task to round off the Foundation path. Take your time — your answers are practice, not a test, and you can carry on whatever you choose.

items.passage: El sábado voy al mercado. Hay frutas y verduras en los puestos. Compro tres manzanas y un kilo de patatas. Pregunto: «¿Cuánto cuesta?» La señora dice: «Todo por cuatro euros.» Le doy cinco euros y ella me devuelve uno.
items.translation: On Saturday I go to the market. There are fruits and vegetables at the stalls. I buy three apples and a kilo of potatoes. I ask: ‘How much does it cost?’ The lady says: ‘Everything for four euros.’ I give her five euros and she gives me one back.

questions.question: ¿Cuánto cuesta todo?
¿Qué compra la persona?

options.text: Tres manzanas y un kilo de patatas
Tres patatas y un kilo de manzanas
Dos manzanas y un kilo de tomates

items.prompt: You have just met a neighbour who speaks only Spanish. Write three short sentences to introduce yourself: say your name (Me llamo …), say where you are from (Soy de …), and finish with Mucho gusto. This is practice, so write what you can and then move on.

Imagine you are in a café in Madrid and the server asks: «¿Qué desea?» Speak your order out loud: greet the server, ask for one coffee, and say thank you. Then play your recording back and tick the things you hear yourself doing.

rubric.text: I greeted the server (hola or buenos días)
I asked for one coffee (un café, por favor)
I said thank you (gracias)
I understood my own recording

checkpoints.title: Telling stories and plans
checkpoints.introduction: The last task of the Developing path. There is no pass or fail: your answers are practice evidence, and whatever you choose, you can carry on.

items.passage: El sábado pasado, Marta y yo fuimos a la playa. Hacía sol y el agua estaba fría. Por la tarde comimos en un restaurante pequeño; pedimos pescado y ensalada. Marta pagó con la tarjeta porque no tenía efectivo. Volvimos a casa a las nueve.
items.translation: Last Saturday, Marta and I went to the beach. The sun was shining and the water was cold. In the afternoon we ate in a small restaurant; we ordered fish and salad. Marta paid by card because she did not have cash. We got home at nine.

questions.question: ¿Qué tiempo hacía el sábado?
¿Por qué pagó Marta con la tarjeta?

options.text: Porque el restaurante no aceptaba tarjetas

items.prompt: Tell a friend what you did last weekend. Write four short sentences: where you went, what you did, what you ate, and what time you came home. Use the past tenses you practised (pretérito or imperfecto). This is practice, so write what you can and then move on.

You are telling a friend about next week. Speak three things out loud: a plan you have, the day you will do it, and where you will go. Use the future (voy a … or iré a …). Then play your recording back and tick the things you hear yourself doing.

rubric.text: I said a plan for next week
I said the day and the place
I used the future (voy a … or iré a …)
I understood my own recording

checkpoints.title: Plans, reasons and decisions
checkpoints.introduction: The last task of the Independent path. There is no pass or fail: your answers are practice evidence, and whatever you choose, you can carry on.

items.passage: El club de baloncesto del barrio abre sus puertas el próximo sábado. Por la mañana, los entrenadores explicarán las normas y harán ejercicios con los nuevos jugadores. Por la tarde habrá un partido amistoso contra un equipo vecino. El club pide a los interesados que lleguen diez minutos antes y que traigan ropa deportiva. La jornada termina con una merienda, porque los socios quieren conocer a los recién llegados.
items.translation: The neighbourhood basketball club opens its doors next Saturday. In the morning, the coaches will explain the rules and do exercises with the new players. In the afternoon there will be a friendly match against a neighbouring team. The club asks those interested to arrive ten minutes early and to bring sports clothes. The day ends with a snack, because the members want to get to know the newcomers.

items.prompt: A friend asks you to explain your plans for the month ahead. Write four or five connected sentences: say one plan you have for work or study, one plan for the weekend, and give a reason for one of them with porque. Use the order words you practised (primero, luego, después, al final). This is practice, so write what you can and then move on.

Tell a friend about a choice you have made for the weekend. Speak three or four sentences: say what you chose, give one reason with porque, and say who you will go with. Try one polite phrase you practised (me gustaría or quería). Then play your recording back and tick the things you hear yourself doing.
